draft.summary: The story adds a registration capability to the existing Quarkus module 'my-app'. The repository index shows no routes, tables or auth files, so persistence, password hashing and a REST endpoint are all new. The only known existing code is a greeting resource and its REST Assured test under com.my.proj.resource. Likely shape: a REST resource for registration, a request/response DTO pair (the response excluding password and hash), a user entity with a unique email and a stored password hash, a repository, and a small service that hashes the password (salted one-way, e.g. bcrypt) before persisting. Which persistence stack and hashing library the project uses is not known from the index (tech_stack is empty), so those choices still need confirming.
affected_packages: com.my.proj.resource (confirmed from existing test path; new registration resource expected here)
com.my.proj.service (proposed, new; registration and password hashing)
com.my.proj.dto (proposed, new; request and response objects)
risks: No persistence layer, datasource configuration or auth setup is indexed, so database dependency, schema creation and test datasource setup may all need to be added; the effort depends on what my-app already declares in its build file, which was not available.
Hashing algorithm and parameters are not specified; a weak or unsalted choice would break the secure-storage requirement.
Password or hash leakage via serialised entities, response DTOs, validation error messages or logs; the response must use a dedicated DTO rather than the entity.
Duplicate-email handling is unspecified; concurrent registrations need a database unique constraint rather than only a check-then-insert, and case handling of emails must be decided.
Package names other than com.my.proj.resource are proposals, not facts from the repository, and should follow existing conventions once confirmed.
Only one test exists (GreetingResourceTest); there are no test helpers, so tests for the new endpoint will need their own setup and database state handling.
